_note: Phase 1 seed. IRA-negotiated drugs are the cleanest starting wedge - documented list price and documented negotiated price, both citable, no AI judgment call needed to prove the model. Common generics are the second wedge (cash-price arbitrage angle). Verify all figures against current source before production use; these are drawn from 2026 reporting and negotiated prices are point-in-time.

ira_negotiated_2026.name: Januvia
ira_negotiated_2026.exploit_angle: patients still on list-price plans or unaware of negotiated price should confirm their plan is passing through the negotiated rate

ira_negotiated_2026.name: Fiasp / NovoLog (insulin)
ira_negotiated_2026.exploit_angle: insulin also has separate $35/month Medicare Part D cap - stack against negotiated price to confirm patient is getting the lower of the two

ira_negotiated_2026.name: Eliquis
ira_negotiated_2026.note: one of the highest-volume Part D drugs by claim count, ~4M beneficiaries

high_volume_generics_watchlist.name: atorvastatin
high_volume_generics_watchlist.note: single most-prescribed drug in Medicare by claim volume; cash price for generic often beats insurance copay at certain pharmacies

2026_price_hike_watchlist.note: ~80 Pfizer drugs saw list price hikes in 2026, median around 4%; hospital-administered drugs like morphine/hydromorphone saw some of the steepest increases (4x+ on certain formulations)

350+ branded medications had planned list price increases for 2026 per 3 Axis Advisors data; these are prime candidates for the monitor job once built, since a rising list price often means the cash-vs-insurance-vs-card arbitrage gap is widening too
